# LexiKey

> Free spelling practice through typing, organised by phonics rule rather than
> word frequency. Built for dyslexic learners and anyone who keeps misspelling
> the same words. Not a words-per-minute trainer.

LexiKey is a web app at https://lexikey.org. It is free, needs no account to
start, and has no timer, leaderboard or reward loop — deliberately, because
those work against the learners it is for.

## How it works

- 1,114 words sorted into 108 phonics groups following the Orton-Gillingham
  approach, the method dyslexia specialists have used for eighty years. A
  session drills one spelling pattern, so learning "shine" transfers to "stripe".
- Two modes: type the word shown on screen, or switch to listening and type
  what is spoken. They are levelled and scored separately because reading and
  hearing a word are different skills.
- Hesitation is tracked, not just errors. A word typed correctly after a long
  pause has not been learned; it returns in later sessions until it is right
  three times running.
- A placement test finds the learner's level so practice starts at the gaps.
- Adjustable font, size, letter spacing, high contrast, dark mode, text-to-speech.

## What it does not do

- It cannot diagnose dyslexia. That needs a qualified assessor.
- It does not teach reading, comprehension or writing — only spelling.
- It does not replace a human tutor, who can read a child's mood and adjust.
  It is what fills the six days between tutoring sessions.

## Pages

- https://lexikey.org/welcome: what LexiKey is and who it is for
- https://lexikey.org/spelling-tutor: honest comparison with hiring a tutor
- https://lexikey.org/how-it-works: the Orton-Gillingham method behind it
- https://lexikey.org/for-parents: for parents of struggling spellers
- https://lexikey.org/for-teachers: classroom use and what it tracks
- https://lexikey.org/: the practice app itself

## Who made it

Built by James Dimonaco, a dyslexic software developer, because writing a word
out ten times never made it stick and years of typing accidentally did.
